body.question: What did the professor say about inheritance?

response:
{"id":12,"answer":"From your notes (entry 5, a lecture takeaway):

- The professor said inheritance is NOT for code reuse — it is for substitutability.
- The rule as stated: if B is-a A, then anywhere A works, B must work. That is the Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP).
- You also noted a follow-up intention: re-read the LSP chapter.

Code-shaped example (general knowledge, not from your notes) — what "substitutability" means in practice:

    class Bird { void fly() { ... } }
    class Penguin extends Bird { void fly() { throw new UnsupportedOperationException(); } }

    void migrate(Bird b) { b.fly(); }   // works for any Bird
    migrate(new Penguin());             // breaks the promise -> bad inheritance

Here Penguin is-a Bird by code, but it cannot stand in wherever a Bird is expected, so the inheritance is for reuse (sharing fly()) rather than substitutability — exactly the distinction the professor drew.

Scope note: only entry 5 in your saved notes speaks to what the professor said about inheritance.
